# Ontology Requirements Specification: Competency Questions for a Rice Pest & Disease Multimodal Knowledge Graph

*Generated by executing the prompt in `rice_mmkg_cq_prompt.md`. All INPUT fields were left as bracketed placeholders, so the defaults stated in the prompt have been applied and every assumption is marked explicitly below.*

---

## 0. Assumptions Applied (placeholders not supplied by the user)

| Placeholder | Value assumed | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Primary end users | Plant pathology researchers, agricultural extension officers, and smart-farming/IoT system developers | Prompt's suggested default |
| Geographic / agroecological scope | Indonesia and mainland/insular Southeast Asia, tropical lowland irrigated and rainfed rice | Prompt's suggested default |
| Pests/diseases in scope | Rice blast (*Pyricularia oryzae* / *Magnaporthe oryzae*), bacterial leaf blight (*Xanthomonas oryzae* pv. *oryzae*), sheath blight (*Rhizoctonia solani*), rice tungro disease (RTBV + RTSV, vectored by *Nephotettix virescens*), brown planthopper (*Nilaparvata lugens*), yellow stem borer (*Scirpophaga incertulas*), rice bug (*Leptocorisa oratorius*), false smut (*Ustilaginoidea virens*) | "Use common major rice pests/diseases" default |
| Datasets per modality | Not supplied; CQs are written to be dataset-agnostic but assume (a) a text corpus of journal articles plus BBPOPT/IRRI-style surveillance bulletins, (b) an annotated field-image collection with region-level labels and IRRI SES severity scores, (c) plot-level IoT agroclimatic time series, (d) variety/genotype and multi-location yield trial tables | Marked assumption |
| Target number of CQs | 36 (within the default 30–40 band), distributed 6 text / 6 image / 5 sensor / 5 genomic / 14 cross-modal (≈39% fusion) | Prompt default |
| Ontology alignment | None supplied; alignment targets are flagged per CQ where relevant (AGROVOC, Crop Ontology CO_320 Rice, Plant Trait Ontology (TO), Plant Ontology (PO), Plant Phenotype Ontology (PPO), Infectious Disease Ontology (IDO) patterns, ENVO, SOSA/SSN, Sequence Ontology (SO), W3C Web Annotation, PROV-O) | Marked assumption |
| Existing drafted CQs to avoid | None supplied | — |

---

## 1. Restatement of Purpose and Scope

This knowledge graph (KG) integrates four modalities — scientific and extension **text**, annotated field **images**, agroclimatic **sensor** time series, and **genomic/tabular** variety records — into a single semantically linked resource for rice pest and disease management in tropical lowland Southeast Asian rice systems. Its purpose is to support early diagnosis, outbreak-risk assessment, and variety-aware management recommendations for plant pathology researchers, extension officers, and precision-agriculture systems. The competency questions below define the functional scope of the KG: each is intended to be answerable, in principle, by a single formal graph query, and collectively they constitute both the ontology requirements and the evaluation criteria for the resulting artefact.

---

## 2. Competency Questions

### 2.a Text-Grounded Competency Questions

| ID | Question | Complexity | Key Entities & Relations | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CQ-TXT-01 | What is the causal agent of rice blast, and which taxonomic synonyms and higher taxa are recorded for it? | Simple | `Disease`, `causedBy`, `Pathogen`, `hasScientificName`, `hasSynonym`, `hasTaxonRank` (align: AGROVOC, NCBITaxon) | Establishes the minimal disease–pathogen backbone on which every other query depends, and resolves the *Magnaporthe*/*Pyricularia* naming ambiguity that fragments literature retrieval. |
| CQ-TXT-02 | Which symptoms are described in the literature as diagnostic for bacterial leaf blight, and on which plant organ and growth stage does each appear? | Simple | `Disease`, `hasSymptom`, `Symptom`, `manifestsOn`, `PlantAnatomicalEntity` (PO), `atGrowthStage` (PPO) | Symptom–organ–stage triples are the pivot on which text descriptions are later aligned to image annotations. |
| CQ-TXT-03 | Which control measures are recommended for sheath blight, of which type (chemical, biological, cultural, host resistance), and in which source and publication year is each recommended? | Relational | `Disease`, `hasControlMeasure`, `ControlMeasure`, `hasActiveIngredient`, `documentedIn`, `Document`, `hasPublicationYear` (PROV-O) | Extension advice must be traceable and datable, since registration status and resistance advisories change over time. |
| CQ-TXT-04 | Which insect vectors are reported to transmit rice tungro disease, in what transmission mode, and which viral component does each transmit? | Relational | `Vector`, `transmits`, `Pathogen`, `hasTransmissionMode`, `partOfDiseaseComplex` (IDO pattern) | Tungro's two-virus, vector-dependent aetiology is the KG's test case for representing multi-agent disease complexes rather than one-pathogen-one-disease. |
| CQ-TXT-05 | Which rice diseases share two or more leaf symptom descriptors and are therefore documented as liable to be confused during field scouting? | Complex-Inferential | `Disease`, `hasSymptom`, `Symptom`, symptom-set intersection, `isDifferentiatedFrom` | Differential-diagnosis support is the core value proposition for extension officers; overlapping symptom sets define where image or sensor evidence must be brought in to disambiguate. |
| CQ-TXT-06 | How has the reported geographic distribution and biotype composition of *Nilaparvata lugens* in Southeast Asia changed across surveillance bulletins published between 2010 and the present? | Complex-Inferential | `PestPopulation`, `hasBiotype`, `reportedIn`, `Region` (ENVO/GeoNames), `observationYear`, temporal aggregation, PROV-O provenance | Biotype shift drives resistance breakdown; the KG must support longitudinal reasoning over dated report assertions rather than storing a single "current" state. |

### 2.b Image-Grounded Competency Questions

| ID | Question | Complexity | Key Entities & Relations | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CQ-IMG-01 | How many annotated images in the KG depict brown planthopper hopperburn, and with what capture device, resolution, and capture date? | Simple | `ImageAsset`, `depicts`, `DamageSign`, `hasCaptureDevice`, `hasResolution`, `hasCaptureDate` | Basic image inventory and technical metadata are prerequisites for any downstream model training or benchmarking use of the KG. |
| CQ-IMG-02 | Which images are labelled as healthy-plant baselines, and how are they distributed across growth stages and canopy views? | Simple | `ImageAsset`, `hasHealthStatus`, `atGrowthStage` (PPO), `hasViewType` | Negative/baseline classes are as necessary as symptom classes for diagnostic evaluation, and their absence is a common defect in agricultural image sets. |
| CQ-IMG-03 | Which annotated image regions are labelled as spindle-shaped lesions with grey centres and necrotic margins, and which annotator and annotation protocol assigned each label? | Relational | `ImageAsset`, `hasRegionOfInterest`, `RegionOfInterest` (W3C Web Annotation `oa:Annotation`, `oa:hasSelector`), `hasVisualDescriptor`, `annotatedBy`, `Agent`, `usedProtocol` (PROV-O) | Region-level, provenance-bearing annotation is what allows a visual descriptor to be linked to a textual symptom term rather than only to a whole-image class label. |
| CQ-IMG-04 | For a given field plot and season, which images were captured at which growth stage, and what disease severity score was assigned to each on the IRRI Standard Evaluation System scale? | Relational | `ImageAsset`, `capturedAt`, `FieldPlot`, `duringSeason`, `hasSeverityScore`, `usesScoringScale` | Severity scoring links image evidence to the ordinal scales used in agronomic trials, making image data interoperable with tabular trial results. |
| CQ-IMG-05 | Which disease × growth-stage × severity combinations are represented by fewer than *N* images, indicating class imbalance in the image collection? | Complex-Inferential | `ImageAsset`, `depicts`, `Disease`, `atGrowthStage`, `hasSeverityScore`, grouped counting | Exposing sampling gaps is an evaluation requirement: a multimodal KG must be able to report on the completeness of its own evidence base. |
| CQ-IMG-06 | For image series captured on the same plot on successive dates, how did the annotated lesion area proportion change between the first and last capture? | Complex-Inferential | `ImageAsset`, `capturedAt`, `FieldPlot`, `hasLesionAreaFraction`, `hasCaptureDate`, temporal ordering and delta computation | Symptom progression, not a single snapshot, is what distinguishes an active epidemic from residual damage, and it requires the KG to order image evidence in time. |

### 2.c Sensor / Environmental-Grounded Competency Questions

| ID | Question | Complexity | Key Entities & Relations | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CQ-ENV-01 | What were the daily mean, minimum, and maximum relative humidity values recorded by the sensor node in plot *P* between two given dates? | Simple | `Sensor` (SOSA), `Observation`, `observedProperty` = RelativeHumidity, `resultTime`, `hasSimpleResult`, `hasFeatureOfInterest` = `FieldPlot` | The elementary time-series retrieval on which all environmental risk reasoning is built. |
| CQ-ENV-02 | Which sensors are hosted on which platform at each monitoring station, which properties does each observe, and at what sampling interval? | Simple | `Platform`, `hosts`, `Sensor`, `observes`, `ObservableProperty`, `hasSamplingInterval`, `deployedAt` (SOSA/SSN) | Deployment metadata determines which sites can support which CQs, and it is required for honest reporting of spatial and temporal coverage. |
| CQ-ENV-03 | Which plots recorded at least five consecutive days with mean relative humidity above 85% and mean air temperature between 25 °C and 30 °C during the vegetative stage of the current season? | Relational | `FieldPlot`, `hasObservation`, threshold predicates over `Observation`, consecutive-day windowing, `atGrowthStage` (PPO) | Conducive-window detection is the standard operational trigger for blast and sheath blight advisories, and it defines the temporal-aggregation capability the KG must expose. |
| CQ-ENV-04 | Rank monitoring sites by cumulative rainfall and by total leaf-wetness duration over the 14 days preceding a given date. | Complex-Inferential | `Site`, `Observation`, `observedProperty` ∈ {Rainfall, LeafWetness}, summation over a sliding window, ranking | Ranking supports prioritisation of scouting effort across sites when extension capacity is limited. |
| CQ-ENV-05 | For each sensor node and month, what proportion of expected observations is missing, and which recorded values fall outside physically plausible bounds? | Complex-Inferential | `Sensor`, `Observation`, expected-vs-actual counting, `hasQualityFlag`, `PlausibilityRange` | Sensor data quality determines whether any fusion CQ built on it is trustworthy; the KG must be able to qualify its own environmental evidence. |

### 2.d Genomic / Tabular-Grounded Competency Questions

| ID | Question | Complexity | Key Entities & Relations | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CQ-GEN-01 | Which resistance genes are carried by a given rice variety (e.g., the pyramided line IRBB60), and against which pathogen does each confer resistance? | Simple | `RiceVariety`, `carriesGene`, `ResistanceGene`, `confersResistanceTo`, `Pathogen` (align: Crop Ontology CO_320, SO) | The variety–gene–pathogen triple is the minimal unit enabling any resistance-aware recommendation. |
| CQ-GEN-02 | On which chromosome and at what map position is each characterised bacterial leaf blight resistance gene located, and is it dominant or recessive? | Simple | `ResistanceGene`, `locatedOn`, `Chromosome`, `hasMapPosition`, `hasInheritanceMode` (SO) | Positional and inheritance data are required if the KG is to be reused by breeding programmes rather than by diagnostics alone. |
| CQ-GEN-03 | Which varieties released in Indonesia after 2015 carry at least two blast resistance genes, and what yield potential and maturity duration are recorded for them? | Relational | `RiceVariety`, `hasReleaseYear`, `hasReleaseCountry`, `carriesGene`, gene counting, `hasYieldPotential`, `hasMaturityDuration` (TO) | Extension recommendations must trade resistance against agronomic performance, so both must be queryable in one traversal. |
| CQ-GEN-04 | Which molecular markers tag the brown planthopper resistance gene *Bph3*, and in which mapping population and study was each validated? | Relational | `Marker`, `tagsGene`, `ResistanceGene`, `validatedIn`, `MappingPopulation`, `reportedIn`, `Document` | Marker-assisted selection workflows need marker provenance, and this CQ tests the text–genomic citation link at the tabular level. |
| CQ-GEN-05 | Comparing multi-location trial records, what is the mean and variance of yield for varieties grouped by their resistance-gene pyramid against *Xanthomonas oryzae* pv. *oryzae*? | Complex-Inferential | `TrialRecord`, `ofVariety`, `atLocation`, `hasYield`, `carriesGene`, grouping and aggregation | Demonstrates that the tabular modality supports statistical comparison, not merely record lookup, which is a prerequisite for evidence-based variety advice. |

### 2.e Cross-Modal / Fusion Competency Questions

| ID | Question | Complexity | Key Entities & Relations | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CQ-MM-01 | For each textual symptom descriptor recorded for rice blast, which annotated image regions provide corresponding visual evidence, and how many images support each descriptor? | Relational (Text × Image) | `Symptom`, `hasVisualDescriptor`, `RegionOfInterest`, `visuallyEvidencedBy`, `ImageAsset`, `depicts`, counting | This is the foundational text–image grounding link: without it the KG is a text database and an image folder side by side. |
| CQ-MM-02 | For every image with a confirmed sheath blight diagnosis, what were the mean temperature, relative humidity, and leaf-wetness duration recorded in the same plot during the seven days preceding capture? | Relational (Image × Sensor) | `ImageAsset`, `capturedAt`, `FieldPlot`, `hasObservation`, `Observation`, temporal window relative to `hasCaptureDate` | Co-locating and co-timing visual evidence with environmental context is the precondition for any empirical statement about conducive conditions. |
| CQ-MM-03 | Given a leaf image annotated with spindle-shaped grey-centred lesions, and sensor readings of relative humidity above 90% with night temperatures of 22–28 °C at the same plot, which disease is the most likely diagnosis, and which literature source states the conducive range that supports this inference? | Complex-Inferential (Image × Sensor × Text) | `RegionOfInterest`, `hasVisualDescriptor`, `Symptom`, `indicativeOf`, `Disease`, `hasConduciveCondition`, `EnvironmentalCondition`, `Observation`, `documentedIn` | The canonical diagnostic fusion query: it exercises visual evidence, environmental corroboration, and literature justification in a single answer. |
| CQ-MM-04 | For plots where images show hopperburn damage, what variety was planted, which brown planthopper resistance genes does that variety carry, and did the recorded temperature and nitrogen-application records fall in ranges known to favour planthopper build-up? | Complex-Inferential (Image × Genomic × Sensor × Tabular) | `ImageAsset`, `depicts`, `DamageSign`, `FieldPlot`, `plantedWith`, `RiceVariety`, `carriesGene`, `Observation`, `hasAgronomicPractice` | Damage on a nominally resistant variety is the signature of resistance breakdown or biotype shift; distinguishing that from agronomic causes requires all four modalities at once. |
| CQ-MM-05 | Which resistance genes are reported in the literature as effective against a specified pathogen race or biotype, and which varieties in the KG actually carry those genes? | Relational (Text × Genomic) | `Document`, `assertsEffectivenessOf`, `ResistanceGene`, `againstRace`, `PathogenRace`, `RiceVariety`, `carriesGene` | Bridges published pathology findings to the deployable germplasm inventory, which is the practical output extension services need. |
| CQ-MM-06 | Under which recorded environmental conditions have plots planted with *Xa21*-carrying varieties nonetheless registered confirmed bacterial leaf blight observations? | Complex-Inferential (Sensor × Genomic × Image/Observation) | `FieldPlot`, `plantedWith`, `RiceVariety`, `carriesGene`, `hasDiseaseObservation`, `Observation`, condition profiling | Directly addresses the Sensor × Genomic pairing, which is the linkage most often left empty in multimodal agricultural KGs. |
| CQ-MM-07 | Within the same season and agroecological zone, how do image-derived mean severity scores compare between plots planted with resistant versus susceptible varieties for a given disease? | Complex-Inferential (Image × Genomic × Tabular) | `FieldPlot`, `plantedWith`, `RiceVariety`, `hasResistanceStatus`, `ImageAsset`, `hasSeverityScore`, grouped aggregation, `inZone` (ENVO) | Converts image annotations into an evidence stream capable of validating or falsifying claimed varietal resistance under field conditions. |
| CQ-MM-08 | For each disease, which literature-stated conducive environmental thresholds were actually exceeded at a given site during the current season, and on which dates? | Complex-Inferential (Text × Sensor) | `Disease`, `hasConduciveCondition`, `EnvironmentalCondition`, `hasThresholdValue`, `Observation`, threshold comparison over time | Operationalises published epidemiological knowledge as an executable early-warning rule set rather than as prose. |
| CQ-MM-09 | Across all recorded seasons, which combinations of environmental variables in the 14 days preceding a confirmed, image-documented blast outbreak occur most frequently, ranked by frequency and by the proportion of conducive windows that were actually followed by an outbreak? | Complex-Inferential (Sensor × Image × Text, four-way with variety context) | `OutbreakEvent`, `confirmedBy`, `ImageAsset`, `diagnosedAs`, `Disease`, `precededBy`, `Observation`, frequency and conditional-rate aggregation | Supplies the empirical basis for risk models and, critically, reports false-positive rates rather than only conducive-condition counts. |
| CQ-MM-10 | Given a diagnosis confirmed from field imagery in a specified plot, which literature-recommended control measures are applicable, and which of them are redundant or contraindicated given the resistance genes carried by the variety planted there? | Relational (Image × Text × Genomic) | `ImageAsset`, `diagnosedAs`, `Disease`, `hasControlMeasure`, `ControlMeasure`, `FieldPlot`, `plantedWith`, `carriesGene`, `contraindicatedFor` | This is the end-to-end decision-support path the KG exists to serve, from visual detection to variety-aware recommendation. |
| CQ-MM-11 | For any given diagnostic conclusion in the KG, what is the complete evidence chain — image and its annotator, supporting sensor observations, cited literature, and variety record — and what confidence or agreement level is attached to it? | Complex-Inferential (four-way, provenance) | `Diagnosis`, `wasDerivedFrom`, `Entity`, `wasAttributedTo`, `Agent`, `wasGeneratedBy`, `Activity` (PROV-O), `hasConfidenceLevel` | Auditable provenance across modalities is what makes the KG citable and reusable by the international research community. |
| CQ-MM-12 | For plots with a confirmed outbreak, how many days elapsed between the onset of a literature-defined conducive environmental window and the first image in which symptoms were annotated? | Complex-Inferential (Sensor × Text × Image, temporal) | `ConduciveWindow`, `hasStartDate`, `ImageAsset`, `hasCaptureDate`, `firstSymptomObservation`, interval computation | Quantified warning lead time is the single most decision-relevant number for extension services and the clearest demonstration of temporal cross-modal reasoning. |
| CQ-MM-13 | Which pest and disease co-occurrences are evidenced in the same plot within the same 14-day window by both image annotations and textual scouting reports, and do the two sources agree? | Relational (Image × Text, spatio-temporal) | `FieldPlot`, `ImageAsset`, `depicts`, `ScoutingReport`, `reports`, `Pest`, `Disease`, temporal-window co-occurrence, `agreesWith` | Co-infection and vector–disease co-occurrence (e.g., green leafhopper with tungro) are commonly missed by single-source pipelines, and cross-source agreement is a direct KG quality measure. |
| CQ-MM-14 | Which diseases represented in the KG lack image evidence, lack sensor coverage at any location where they have been reported, or lack any variety with a documented resistance gene against them? | Complex-Inferential (four-way coverage) | `Disease`, negation over `depicts`, `hasObservation`, `confersResistanceTo`, `reportedAt`, `Site` | Makes the KG's own multimodal coverage gaps explicit and queryable, which is required both for iterative population and for honest reporting of limitations in publication. |

## 3. Modality-Pair Coverage Summary

| Modality combination | CQ IDs | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Text only | CQ-TXT-01 … CQ-TXT-06 | 6 |
| Image only | CQ-IMG-01 … CQ-IMG-06 | 6 |
| Sensor only | CQ-ENV-01 … CQ-ENV-05 | 5 |
| Genomic/tabular only | CQ-GEN-01 … CQ-GEN-05 | 5 |
| Text × Image | CQ-MM-01, CQ-MM-13 | 2 |

| Text × Sensor | CQ-MM-08 | 1 |
| Text × Genomic | CQ-MM-05 | 1 |
| Image × Genomic | (covered within CQ-MM-07) | 0 dedicated |

| Text × Image × Sensor | CQ-MM-03, CQ-MM-12 | 2 |
| Image × Sensor × Genomic | CQ-MM-04 | 1 |

| Four-way (Text × Image × Sensor × Genomic/Tabular) | CQ-MM-11, CQ-MM-14 | 2 |

**Coverage gaps visible from this table.** Two pairings are thin. First, **Image × Genomic** has no dedicated two-way CQ; it is exercised only inside the three-way CQ-MM-07, so a dedicated CQ (e.g., "Which visual symptom phenotypes are recorded on varieties carrying a given resistance gene?") should be added if the pairing must be tested in isolation. Second, **Text × Sensor** and **Image × Sensor** each rest on a single CQ, which is adequate given that both are re-tested inside CQ-MM-03, CQ-MM-09 and CQ-MM-12, but leaves little redundancy if either CQ proves infeasible. All four modalities appear in at least eight CQs each.

## 4. Scope Boundary Note

**In scope.** The KG covers named rice pests and diseases of tropical lowland Southeast Asian rice, their causal agents and vectors, their symptoms as described in text and as annotated in field imagery, the plot-level agroclimatic conditions under which they are observed, the rice varieties planted and the resistance genes those varieties carry, and the provenance links that tie any diagnostic conclusion back to its supporting evidence in each modality. It is designed to answer diagnostic, risk-assessment, and variety-aware recommendation questions at the granularity of a field plot and a season.

**Out of scope.** The KG does not model crop physiology or growth simulation beyond phenological stage annotation; it does not represent farm economics, market prices, pesticide registration law, or land tenure; it does not store raw pixel or raw genomic sequence data (only references, derived annotations, and curated genotype assertions); it does not perform image classification or forecasting itself, but rather stores, links, and exposes the evidence that such models consume and produce; and it makes no claims about pests and diseases of crops other than *Oryza sativa*.

**Feasibility flags.** Several CQs should be revisited once actual datasets are confirmed. CQ-MM-02, CQ-MM-03, CQ-MM-09 and CQ-MM-12 all presuppose that images and sensor readings share a resolvable plot identifier and reliable timestamps; public rice image collections are frequently supplied without geolocation or capture date, in which case these CQs are answerable only for a purpose-collected subset. CQ-MM-04 additionally requires nitrogen-application records, which are agronomic-management data not listed among the four stated modalities and may need a separate source. CQ-MM-06, CQ-MM-07 and CQ-MM-09 require that the variety planted in each imaged plot be recorded, which is the single most common missing link between the image and genomic modalities. CQ-TXT-06 and CQ-MM-09 require multi-season historical depth that a newly instrumented site will not possess for some years. Finally, CQ-IMG-06 and CQ-MM-07 assume lesion-area or severity values are attached to image annotations rather than whole-image class labels alone; if only class labels exist, both must be downgraded to categorical comparisons.
